claims.author: cyb3ralbert
claims.harm: A stalled peer that stops responding to getheaders remains connected indefinitely, holding the outbound slot.
claims.quote: With a single outbound peer, a peer that sends one headers message and then stops responding to `getheaders` remains connected for 24 hours under mocktime, whereas master disconnects it after 24 minutes.

status_by.quote: Pushed bf56f4fb83. The presync work is now recorded when the timeout is set, and when it expires the timeout is only renewed if that work has increased since.

claims.status_note: author confirmed and pushed bf56f4fb83 renewing the timeout only if presync work increased

claims.author: cyb3ralbert
claims.question: Whether the Tor/I2P latency scenario is expected to apply when there is only a single outbound peer.
claims.quote: Is the Tor/I2P latency scenario expected to apply when this is the only outbound peer?

status_by.quote: Single outbound peer: nothing in the logic depends on how many outbound peers there are, so a slow Tor/I2P link can hit it with one peer as well

claims.status_note: author explained that logic is independent of peer count

claims.author: cyb3ralbert
claims.question: Whether the eviction was observed on a real node or inferred from expected round-trip times.
claims.quote: Was the eviction observed on a real node, or inferred from expected round-trip times?

status_by.quote: Real node: no, the eviction was not observed on a real node. It is inferred from the ~480 presync round trips on mainnet against the ~22 minute window

claims.status_note: author confirmed it was inferred from mainnet round trips and reproduced in mocktime tests
